parole.significato: adequate [with do (+ genitive) ‘to/for what’] or, proscribed
parole.testo: Internationalism; possibly borrowed from French adéquat, German adäquat, or English adequate, ultimately from Latin adaequātus + -ny. First attested in 1873.

parole.significato: accordion (small, portable, keyed wind instrument)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French accordéon, from German Akkordion. First attested in 1844.

parole.significato: banker (one who conducts the business of banking)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French banquier or German Bankier.

parole.significato: barbican (tower at the entrance to a castle or fortified town)
parole.testo: Internationalism; compare English barbican. Possibly borrowed from French barbacane or German Barbakane, possibly through Spanish barbacana, or borrowed from Italian barbacane. Further etymology uncertain, possibly from Arabic بَرْبَخ (barbaḵ, “aqueduct, sewer”) or Persian بابخانه (bâb-xâne, “gateho

parole.significato: petrol, gasoline
parole.testo: Borrowed from French benzine, from German Benzin. Coined by Eilhardt Mitscherlich in 1833.

parole.significato: bismuth (chemical element, Bi, atomic number 63)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French bismuth, from German Wismut, Wismuth, from Middle High German wismāt, from Latin bisemūtum, from Arabic بِسِيمُوتِيُّون (bisīmūtiyyūn), from Ancient Greek ψιμύθιον (psimúthion, “white lead”). First attested in 1807.

parole.significato: to bombard (to attack something with bombs, artillery shells, or other missiles)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French bombarder or German bombardieren + -ować.

parole.significato: chrysanthemum
parole.testo: Borrowed from French chrysanthème and German Chrysantheme, from Latin chrysanthemum, from Ancient Greek χρυσάνθεμον (khrusánthemon).

parole.significato: to civilize (to introduce or impose the standards of one civilisation upon another civilization, group or person, argua…
parole.testo: Borrowed from French civiliser, German zivilisieren + -ować.

parole.significato: to degenerate (to cause to lose good or desirable qualities)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French dégénérer, German degenerieren + -ować, from Latin dēgenerō.

parole.significato: to demote (to lower the rank or status of)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French dégrader, German degradieren + -ować, from Ecclesiastical Latin dēgradō.

parole.significato: decorative motif, pattern
parole.testo: Borrowed from French décor and German Dekor.

parole.significato: to devalue (to lower or remove the value of something)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French dévaluer, German devaluieren + -ować.

parole.significato: dialect
parole.testo: Borrowed from French dialecte, from German Dialekt, from Ancient Greek διάλεκτος (diálektos).

parole.significato: to dynamize (to make dynamic)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French dynamiser, German dynamisieren + -ować.

parole.significato: to conduct [with instrumental ‘something’] (to direct, as the leader in the performance of a musical composition)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French diriger, German dirigieren + -ować, from Latin dīrigō.

parole.significato: disputation, dispute
parole.testo: Borrowed from French dispute and German Disput.

parole.significato: to experiment, to experimentalize (to conduct an experiment)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French expérimenter, German experimentieren + -ować, from Latin experīmentum, from experior.

parole.significato: if and only if, iff, material equivalence
parole.testo: Internationalism; possibly borrowed from French équivalence, or German Äquivalenz, ultimately from Latin aequivaleō.

parole.significato: equivalence, equivalency, equivalent
parole.testo: Borrowed from French équivalent or German Äquivalent.

parole.significato: to emancipate (to set free from the power of another)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French émanciper, German emanzipieren + -ować, from Latin ēmancipō.

parole.significato: emigrant
parole.testo: Borrowed from French émigrant and German Emigrant, from Latin ēmigrāns.

parole.significato: to erode (to wear away (something) by abrasion, corrosion or chemical reaction)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French éroder, German erodieren + -ować, from Latin ērōdō.

parole.significato: philharmonic, philharmonic orchestra, symphony orchestra
parole.testo: Borrowed from French philharmonie and German Philharmonie, from Ancient Greek φιλία (philía) + ἁρμονία (harmonía).

parole.significato: to finalize (to make final or firm; to finish or complete)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French finaliser, German finalisieren + -ować.

parole.significato: inflection
parole.testo: Borrowed from French flexion or German Flexion, from Latin flexiō.

parole.significato: to fluctuate (to vary irregularly; to swing)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French fluctuer, German fluktuieren + -ować, from Latin flūctuō.

parole.significato: format, size
parole.testo: Borrowed from French format, from German Format, from New Latin liber fōrmātus.

parole.significato: to frustrate (to cause stress or annoyance)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French frustrer, German frustrieren + -ować, from Latin frūstrō.

parole.significato: fusion
parole.testo: Borrowed from French fusion, German Fusion, from Latin fūsiō.

parole.significato: to ignore (to pretend to not notice someone or something)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French ignorer, German ignorieren + -ować, from Latin ignōrāre.

parole.significato: to impregnate, to saturate
parole.testo: Borrowed from French imprégner, German imprägnieren + -ować, from Latin impraegnō.

parole.significato: to inaugurate (to dedicate ceremoniously; to initiate something in a formal manner)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French inaugurer, German inaugurieren + -ować, from Latin inaugurō.

parole.significato: to infiltrate (to surreptitiously penetrate, enter or gain access to)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French infiltrer, German infiltrieren + -ować.

parole.significato: to incubate (to brood, raise, or maintain eggs, organisms, or living tissue through the provision of ideal environmenta…
parole.testo: Borrowed from French incuber, German inkubieren + -ować, from Latin incubō.

parole.significato: institution (a long-established organization or type of organization, particularly one involved with education, public…
parole.testo: Internationalism; possibly borrowed from French institution, German Institution, or English institution, ultimately from Latin īnstitūtiō. First attested in 1556–1557. Compare Silesian instytucyjŏ.

parole.significato: caffeine
parole.testo: Borrowed from French caféine or German Koffein.

parole.significato: to collaborate (to voluntarily cooperate treasonably, as with an enemy occupation force in one's country)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French collaborer, German kollaborieren + -ować, from Latin collabōrō.

parole.significato: to colonize (to settle a place with colonists, and hence make a place into a colony)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French coloniser, German kolonisieren + -ować.

parole.significato: company, fellowship, group
parole.testo: Borrowed from French compagnie and German Kompanie, from Italian compagnia.

parole.significato: to concentrate (to bring to, or direct toward, a common center; to unite more closely; to gather into one body, mass, o…
parole.testo: Borrowed from French concentrer, German konzentrieren + -ować.

parole.significato: to confront (to set a thing side by side with; to compare)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French confronter, German konfrontieren + -ować, from Medieval Latin confrontare.

parole.significato: concrete; specific (particular, specific, rather than general)
parole.testo: Internationalism; possibly borrowed from French concret or German konkret, ultimately from Latin concrētus + -ny. First attested in 1838. Compare Kashubian kònkretny and Silesian kōnkretny.

parole.significato: to contest (to call into question; to oppose)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French contester, German kontestieren + -ować, from Latin contestor.

parole.significato: to corrupt (to cause to act dishonestly in return for money or personal gain)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French corrompre, German korrumpieren + -ować, from Latin corrumpō.

parole.significato: to amass, to accumulate, to cumulate
parole.testo: Borrowed from French cumuler, German kumulieren + -ować, from Latin cumulō.

parole.significato: landau (a type of lightweight, four-wheeled carriage)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French landau, named after the German city of Landau.

parole.significato: to authorize, to justify, to warrant (to grant (someone) the permission or power necessary to do (something))
parole.testo: Borrowed from French légitimer, German legitimieren + -ować, from Medieval Latin legitimare, from Latin lēgitimus.

parole.significato: methane (CH₄)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French méthane and German Methan.

parole.significato: hoaxer, mystifier
parole.testo: Borrowed from French mystificateur or German Mystifikator.

parole.significato: for example, for instance (as an example)
parole.testo: Literally, “for example”. Calque of French par exemple and German zum Beispiel. Compare Kashubian na przëkłôd.

parole.significato: to nationalize (to make a private asset public)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French nationaliser, German nationalisieren + -ować.

parole.significato: to narcotize (to use a narcotic in order to make (someone) drowsy or insensible; to anesthetize, to drug)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French narcotiser, German narkotisieren + -ować.

parole.significato: responsible (having or evidential of good judgment in decision-making)
parole.testo: From odpowiedzieć + -alny. Calque of French responsable, German verantwortlich/verantwortungsvoll, and Russian отве́тственный (otvétstvennyj). First attested in the 17th centeury.

parole.significato: fuel, propellant (substance consumed to provide energy through combustion, or through chemical or nuclear reaction)
parole.testo: From palić + -iwo. Calque of French combustible and German Brennstoff, coined with the widespread use of steam machines. First attested in 1783.

parole.significato: to position
parole.testo: Possibly from French positionner, German positionieren + -ować.

parole.significato: claimant, pretendant, pretender
parole.testo: Borrowed from French prétendant or German Prätendent.

parole.significato: publicist
parole.testo: Borrowed from French publiciste and German Publizist.

parole.significato: to ration (to portion out (especially during a shortage of supply); to limit access to)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French rationner and/or German rationieren + -ować.

parole.significato: reference (an object containing information which refers to data stored elsewhere, as opposed to containing the data it…
parole.testo: Borrowed from French référence and/or German Referenz.

parole.significato: to regenerate (to revitalize)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French régénérer, German regenerieren + -ować, from Latin regenerō.

parole.significato: to abide by, to respect (to have regard for something, to observe a custom, practice, rule or right)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French respecter, German respektieren + -ować, from Latin respectō.

parole.significato: to reciprocate (to counter, retort or retaliate)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French se revancher, German revanchieren sich + -ować.

parole.significato: synonym
parole.testo: From równoznaczny + -ik. Calque of French équivalent and German Äquivalent.

parole.significato: to sanction (to give official authorization or approval to)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French sanctionner, German sanktionieren + -ować.

parole.significato: chamotte (a ceramic raw material with a high percentage of silica and alumina)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French chamotte, from German Schamotte, of uncertain origin.

parole.significato: to valorize (to fix the price of (something) at an artificially high level)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French valoriser, German valorisieren + -ować.

parole.significato: zigzag (line)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French zigzag, from German Zickzack.
